title: Israel’s VCs see opportunity for challengers in Nvidia’s turmoil
lede: Israeli investors say Jensen Huang's exit could give Nvidia's challengers room, even as they worry about a tech scene closely tied to the company.

points: Nvidia's 2019 purchase of Mellanox for $6.9 billion made Israel its largest R&D base outside the U.S.
The company employs 6,000 people there and planned a campus in northern Israel.
Vertex Ventures' Yanai Oron says slower decisions could help rivals, though lower AI spending would shrink the prize.
Selah Ventures' Adi Levanon says challengers must prove better economics, as a leadership change alone will not win them business.
Two Israelis, Johny Srouji and Michael Kagan, are among the names floated as successor.

sections.text: Startups building AI chips and inference software get a window to compete on cost while Nvidia settles its leadership.
